transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I can’t seem to stay focused on what I’m doing at the machines long enough to do the job the way they need me to. It's gotten really bad lately with the new lines at the plant, and I'm terrified I'm going to lose my job if I can't get a grip on this.
Did these focus problems start only after the new lines at work and the fear of losing your job, or have you had similar attention problems since childhood or in other parts of your life too?

It actually goes way back to when I was a kid, even though it only blew up at work about 14 months ago when the new lines started. Back in elementary school, I was always the kid who couldn't stay in my seat, blurted out answers, and got in trouble for talking nonstop. It's just that now, it's affecting my job instead of just my report cards.
Did you also have trouble with restlessness, fidgeting, interrupting others, or acting before thinking as a child, or was it mainly just trouble paying attention?

Oh, I definitely had all of those issues as a kid, too. Back in elementary school, I couldn't stay in my seat, was constantly wandering around the classroom, and would blurt out answers or talk nonstop. It was definitely a lot of physical restlessness and interrupting, not just trouble paying attention.
Did these attention and restlessness problems continue through your teens and adulthood, or did they mostly go away for long periods and only come back recently?

They never actually went away; I've had these tendencies my whole life, through high school and my early years at the factory. I managed to get by back then because I chose hands-on tasks and worked alone, so it didn't cause major problems. It only became a massive crisis about 14 months ago when the plant upgraded to faster lines with strict procedures that I couldn't just bypass.
Before age 12, did these attention, impulsivity, or hyperactivity problems cause problems in more than one setting, such as at school and at home?

I definitely had those issues at school, like not staying in my seat, blurting out answers, and wandering around the classroom. I'm not really sure or don't remember if it caused major problems at home or in other places back then, though.
Do you remember these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors causing problems at home too before age 12, or was it mostly just at school?

It was definitely school where it caused the most trouble, since I was always getting scolded for not staying in my seat, blurting out answers, wandering around, and talking nonstop. I don't really recall it being as much of an issue at home, or at least school is what stands out most in my memory from back then.
Did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors also cause clear problems at home or in other settings before age 12, or was it mainly only at school?

It was really just school that I remember having major issues with before I was 12. I was always getting in trouble there for wandering around the classroom, blurting out answers, and never staying in my seat. I honestly don't recall it causing much trouble at home.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors cause clear problems in more than one setting, such as both at school and at home, or was it mainly only at school?

Yes, it was definitely prominent at school, where I was always getting in trouble for wandering around, blurting out answers, and not staying in my seat. I'm really not sure how much it affected things at home, as I mostly just remember it being a major problem in the classroom.
Before age 12, did your restlessness, impulsivity, or trouble paying attention also cause clear problems at home or in other places besides school, or was it mainly only at school?

Before age 12, it was definitely school where I had the most trouble, constantly getting yelled at for wandering the classroom, blurting out answers, and talking nonstop. I don't really remember it causing any clear problems at home. It was mostly just a major issue in the classroom.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors cause clear problems in at least two settings, such as both school and home, or was it mainly only at school?

It was really just at school where I remember having major problems, like constantly getting in trouble for wandering around, talking nonstop, and not staying in my seat. I don't recall it causing any real issues at home or in other places back then. So as far as I can remember, it was pretty much just a school thing.
Before age 12, did your attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in at least two settings, such as both school and home, or was it mainly only at school?

Like I said, I definitely remember it being a major problem at school because I was always getting in trouble for wandering around, talking nonstop, and not staying in my seat. I really don't recall it being much of an issue at home, though. It was pretty much just at school as far as I can remember.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in at least two settings, such as both school and home, or was it mainly only at school?

It was really just at school where those behaviors got me into trouble. I don't remember having any real problems at home before I was 12, but in elementary school I was constantly being scolded for wandering around, blurting out answers, and talking nonstop.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors also clearly cause problems at home or with friends, or was it mainly only at school?

I'm not entirely sure and I don't clearly remember if those behaviors caused major problems at home or with my friends back then. I mostly just remember getting in trouble at school for wandering around, talking nonstop, and not staying in my seat.
Before age 12, did your attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in any other setting besides school, such as at home, with friends, or in activities outside of school?
I'm really not sure or don't recall having any major issues in other settings like at home or with friends back then. School was definitely where I got in trouble the most for my behavior.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in any setting besides school, such as at home, with friends, or in activities outside of school?
I honestly don't recall having any major issues at home or with friends before I was 12. School is really the only place I remember getting into trouble for my behavior back then.

Before age 12, did your attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors cause clear problems in more than one setting, such as both at school and at home or with friends, or was it mainly only at school?

I mostly remember these issues causing trouble at school, like wandering around the classroom and talking during lessons. I'm really not sure or don't remember if it was a big problem at home or with friends back then.
Did these attention or restlessness problems also clearly cause trouble at home, with friends, or in other settings before age 12, or was it mainly only at school?

Before age 12, those problems were definitely most noticeable and caused the most trouble at school, where I was always getting scolded for not staying in my seat, wandering around, and talking nonstop. I really don't recall it causing as much obvious trouble at home or with my friends back then.

Do you remember these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors causing clear problems in at least two settings before age 12, such as both at school and at home or with friends? Or was it mainly only at school?

I really only remember it being a major issue at school. In elementary school, I was constantly getting in trouble because I couldn't stay in my seat, blurted out answers, and was always wandering around or talking during lessons.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in any setting besides school, such as at home or with friends? Or was it mainly only at school?

It was mainly only at school that I remember having real problems. I was always getting in trouble there for wandering around, blurting out answers, and not staying in my seat, but I don't recall it causing issues at home or with my friends.
Did your attention or restlessness problems clearly cause trouble in at least one other setting besides school before age 12, such as at home or with friends? Or was it only a school problem?
I'm not quite sure and don't clearly remember if it caused major issues at home or with friends back then. I mostly just remember getting in trouble at school for wandering around and talking.

Before age 12, did your attention, restlessness, or impulsive behavior clearly cause problems in more than one setting, such as both school and home or with friends, or was it mainly only a school problem?

I definitely remember it being a big issue at school, like wandering around the classroom and talking nonstop. But I'm not really sure or don't recall if it caused major problems at home or with friends back then.
Before age 12, did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in any setting besides school, such as at home or with friends?
I'm not really sure and don't clearly remember having those specific problems at home or with friends back then. I mostly just remember getting in trouble at school.
Before age 12, did your attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems in more than one setting, such as both at school and at home or with friends?

I definitely had a lot of trouble at school, like wandering around the classroom and talking nonstop in elementary school. However, I'm really not sure or don't recall if it caused any major problems at home or with friends back then.
Do these attention, restlessness, or impulsive behaviors still cause problems in more than one setting now, such as at work and at home or in social situations, or is it mainly only at work?

Yes, it definitely affects my life outside of work too, not just at the plant. Even on my days off at home, I can't just sit quietly to watch a show or read a book because I'm always getting up, fiddling with my phone, or talking over the TV. While work is where I'm in the most trouble right now with the performance plan, it's honestly exhausting because I can never just relax at home either.
Do you also have ongoing problems with inattention, restlessness, or impulsive behavior in other parts of life, like at home or in social situations, not just at work?

Yes, it definitely affects me at home and in social situations too. Even on my days off, I can't sit quietly to watch a show or read because I feel this constant need to move, fidget with my phone, or get up. Plus, when I'm around others, I tend to talk excessively and constantly interrupt people mid-sentence.
Have these attention, restlessness, or impulsive behaviors caused clear problems in at least two areas of your life since childhood, such as at work and at home or in social situations?

Yes, they definitely have. Since childhood, it caused constant trouble at school with teachers scolding me for wandering and talking, and now at work, it's led to write-ups, safety issues, and a performance plan. In my personal life, it makes it impossible to relax because I'm always fidgeting, talking over the TV, or interrupting people during conversations.
Do you also often make careless mistakes, lose things, or forget appointments and daily tasks because you’re distracted, or is the main problem mostly restlessness and interrupting?

It is definitely a mix of both. On one hand, I am highly distractible and get pulled away by forklifts or my own thoughts, which makes me forget daily tasks like bringing my lockout tag or calling my supervisor back. On the other hand, I have this intense physical restlessness where my body feels like it's buzzing, and I constantly interrupt people or cut them off mid-sentence.

Do your hyperactive or impulsive behaviors ever get you into trouble at work or with other people, like acting without thinking, interrupting, or doing things that are risky or disruptive? Or is it mostly just trouble staying focused and sitting still?

Yes, my impulsivity definitely gets me in trouble beyond just focus issues. I constantly interrupt coworkers mid-sentence and even reach over to adjust their machines without asking, and I've been written up for disrupting briefings by talking too much and pacing. I even narrowly avoided a serious accident recently when I impulsively stepped into a restricted area without waiting for a safety lockout.

Do you often act without thinking in ways that cause problems, like interrupting others, blurting things out, or doing risky things on impulse, or is your main issue just being unable to focus and sit still?

I definitely struggle with both. I act on impulse all the time, like cutting people off mid-sentence, jumping into conversations, adjusting coworkers' machines without asking, and even stepping into a restricted area without waiting for a safety lockout. But at the same time, I also struggle severely with staying focused, fidgeting, and being completely unable to sit still.
Did these attention, restlessness, and impulsive symptoms begin before age 12 and continue more or less continuously into adulthood, or did they only start later in life?

Yes, they definitely started before I was 12, all the way back in elementary school. I was always the kid who couldn't stay in my seat, constantly blurted out answers, and got in trouble for wandering around the classroom and talking nonstop. Those behaviors have pretty much continued my whole life right into adulthood.
